title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 183 (Power of Board and other persons to make contributions to National Defence Fund, etc.)

content.overview: Section 183 provides that the Board of Directors of any company or any person or authority exercising the powers of the Board of Directors of a company, or of the company in general meeting, may contribute such amount as it thinks fit to the National Defence Fund or any other Fund approved by the Central Government for the purpose of national defence. The total amount so contributed must be disclosed in the profit and loss account.
content.glance: Board (or person/authority exercising Board powers, or company in general meeting) may contribute any amount it thinks fit to National Defence Fund or CG-approved national-defence fund; total disclosed in P&L; no member-threshold gate like s. 181.
content.study: The Board of Directors of any company or any person or authority exercising the powers of the Board of Directors of a company, or of the company in general meeting, may contribute such amount as it thinks fit to the National Defence Fund or any other Fund approved by the Central Government for the purpose of national defence. Every company shall disclose in its profits and loss account the total amount or amounts contributed by it to the Fund referred to during the financial year to which the amount relates. No prior general-meeting permission is required by this section for any amount. The power is distinct from the charitable-contribution regime in section 181 (with its 5% average-net-profits gate) and from political contributions under section 182. Current-law framing: confirm the recipient is the National Defence Fund or a Central Government-approved national-defence fund; Board (or equivalent) may decide the amount; ensure P&L disclosure.

sections.heading: Power
sections.body: Board of Directors, or any person or authority exercising Board powers, or the company in general meeting, may contribute such amount as it thinks fit.

sections.heading: Permitted Funds
sections.body: National Defence Fund or any other Fund approved by the Central Government for the purpose of national defence.

sections.heading: Disclosure
sections.body: Total amount contributed under the section during the financial year must be disclosed in the profit and loss account.

sections.heading: No Member Gate
sections.body: Unlike s. 181, there is no percentage-of-profits threshold requiring prior general-meeting permission.

provisions.title: Power of Board and other persons to make contributions to National Defence Fund, etc.

examples.title: Board contribution to National Defence Fund
examples.body: The Board resolves to contribute a substantial sum to the National Defence Fund and discloses it in the P&L. Section 183 authorises the contribution without a prior ordinary resolution of members.

examples.title: Unapproved fund
examples.body: A contribution to a private charity labelled for defence but not approved by the Central Government as a national-defence fund does not fall under s. 183; s. 181 may apply instead if it is a bona fide charitable fund.

hypotheticals.question: Is a prior ordinary resolution required if the defence-fund contribution exceeds 5% of average net profits?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 183 has no percentage gate. The 5% average-net-profits rule is specific to s. 181 charitable contributions and does not apply to National Defence Fund contributions under s. 183.

distinctions.title: National Defence Fund (s. 183) vs charitable contributions (s. 181)
distinctions.left: Any amount the Board thinks fit; no member threshold
distinctions.right: Bona fide charitable funds; prior ordinary resolution above 5% of average net profits

misconceptions.trap: Defence-fund contributions need the same member approval as large charitable gifts under s. 181.
misconceptions.correction: Section 183 allows the Board to contribute any amount it thinks fit to approved national-defence funds without a member-threshold gate.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 183 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm National Defence Fund or CG-approved fund. II. Note Board power as to amount. III. Ensure P&L disclosure. IV. Distinguish s. 181. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Fund identity; Board decision; disclosure; precise relief.
